name: Fara 1.5
tagline: Microsoft's computer-use agent family goes MIT — screenshots in, clicks out, weights on your disk
description: A family of computer-use agent models from Microsoft Research AI Frontiers — 4B, 9B, and 27B, built on Qwen3.5 — that automate web tasks from vision alone: the model looks at browser screenshots and emits coordinate-grounded actions (click, type, scroll) with no DOM access required. The GitHub repo ships the full harness — agent runtime, WebEval benchmarking framework, docs, and a transparency note. Fara1.5-27B posts 89.3% on WebVoyager and 72.3% on Online-Mind2Web; the 9B is close behind at a fraction of the footprint.
why: Computer-use agents have been the most conspicuously closed corner of the agent stack — the frontier labs sell theirs by the token. Here the whole family is downloadable, and the licensing is as clean as we could verify: the GitHub LICENSE is the standard, unmodified MIT text (1,066 bytes, copyright Microsoft), read directly from a fresh clone. The HF weights repos are tagged MIT and the card says MIT outright, though none of the three weights repos ships a standalone LICENSE file — the same gap we track on Qwen3-Coder-Next and friends. An open CUA you can fine-tune on your own workflows is a genuinely new capability class for this catalog.
useCases: Self-hosted browser automation — form-filling, bookings, structured web tasks — without a per-token meter
Fine-tuning a computer-use agent on your own internal tools and flows, at 4B/9B sizes that fit real budgets
Studying and benchmarking CUA behavior with the bundled WebEval framework
audience: Agent builders, RPA refugees, and researchers who want a computer-use baseline they can actually inspect

setup.requirements: Python via uv; weights from HF (27B is ~55GB in 10 shards, 9B and 4B much lighter); a browser environment for the agent loop. Hosted inference via Microsoft Foundry if you'd rather not serve it

license.notes: Re-verified 2026-11-01. Code: LICENSE read from a fresh clone of microsoft/fara — standard, unmodified MIT text, 1,066 bytes, copyright Microsoft, no rider; unchanged since 2026-09-07. Weights: microsoft/Fara1.5-27B, -9B, and -4B on HF each carry the mit license tag, and the file listings (22, 17, and 14 files) contain no standalone LICENSE file — the same declared-but-fileless gap we flag on Qwen3-Coder-Next, KAT-Coder-V2.5-Dev, and Ling-3.0-flash, and the verdict follows that precedent. Release date settled: the repo README records 'Fara1.5 released' on 2026-07-22 and the weights repos date from late July (the 'May 21' date seen on one card rendering is unsupported). Note the models are built on Qwen3.5 (Apache-2.0 lineage), so obligations stay permissive either way. We'd like to see the file appear.

tally.stars: 6.2k GitHub stars and 605 forks; HF likes 298 (27B), 60 (9B), 59 (4B), with roughly 2.4k–3.0k downloads last month per size
tally.lastActivity: Fara1.5 family released July 22, 2026; weights repos last updated July 27; GitHub repo last pushed September 22, 2026

limitations: Computer-use benchmarks are notoriously brittle — 89% on WebVoyager does not mean 89% on your intranet app; vision-only perception means it can misread dense UIs; and an agent that clicks things on the live web deserves sandboxing and human oversight, which the repo's own transparency note is candid about.
take: The company that sells Copilot subscriptions just handed out MIT-licensed computer-use agents in three sizes. Whatever the strategy, the result is the first serious open CUA family — and the fine-tuning experiments start now.
